blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how your favorite applications save your progress or load data from a file? This lesson will explore how programs read from and write to files, and why these operations can be slower than computations done in memory.

blocks.markdown: In programming, files are used to store data permanently. Unlike variables, which lose their data when a program ends, files retain their data. This makes them essential for tasks like saving user progress in a game or storing configuration settings.

blocks.title: File I/O
blocks.text: File Input/Output (I/O) refers to the process of reading data from and writing data to files. This involves opening a file, performing read/write operations, and then closing the file to release system resources.

blocks.markdown:
To perform file I/O in most programming languages, you typically follow these steps:
1. Open the file.
2. Read from or write to the file.
3. Close the file to free up system resources.

blocks.title: Reading a Text File
blocks.prompt: Let's read the contents of a text file named `example.txt`.

steps.text: Open the file in read mode.
Read the contents of the file.

blocks.answer: The file's contents are stored in the variable `content`.

blocks.title: Writing to a Text File
blocks.prompt: Write the string 'Hello, World!' to a file named `output.txt`.

steps.text: Open the file in write mode.
Write the string to the file.

blocks.answer: The string 'Hello, World!' is written to `output.txt`.

blocks.title: Importance of Closing Files
blocks.text: Always close files after performing I/O operations to release system resources and avoid potential data loss or corruption.

blocks.markdown: File I/O operations can fail for various reasons, such as the file not existing or lacking permissions to read/write. Handling these errors gracefully is crucial to prevent program crashes.

rows: Prepare the file for reading or writing.
blocks.caption: Basic File Operations

blocks.markdown: Compared to in-memory computations, I/O operations are slower because they involve physical storage devices. Accessing data from a hard drive or SSD takes more time than accessing data stored in RAM.

blocks.title: Handling Missing Files
blocks.text: Always check if a file exists before attempting to read it, and handle the case where it might be missing to avoid runtime errors.

points: File I/O involves opening, reading/writing, and closing files.
Closing files is essential to free up resources and prevent data corruption.
I/O operations are slower than in-memory computations due to physical storage access.
